feeds.title: Chesapeake Light Craft Blog
feeds.description: Chesapeake Light Craft helps you build boats. If this is your first boatbuilding project, you'll find on this site a trove of boat designs conceived just for you, and more importantly, an organization devoted to helping builders of all skill levels. If you've never built a boat before in your life, Chesapeake Light Craft places at your disposal all of the resources to make it the experience of a lifetime.

feeds.title: DIY Wood Boat Blog
feeds.description: The Wooden Boat Blog brings you the latest stories from other boat restorers and builders plus advice and tips on building and restoring Wooden Boats, and boats for sale. Over my many years of messing about in wooden boats, the author has built them, repaired them, and renovated them.

feeds.title: Small Boats Monthly
feeds.description: Small Boats Magazine is a monthly web-based magazine dedicated to owners and users of boats that can be stored and maintained at an average-size home. It features a range of designs for oar, paddle, power, and sail. Each issue of Small Boats Magazine includes two in-depth boat profiles, as well as rich coverage of gear, technique, adventure and travel narrative, and reader-built boats. The magazine maintains a sensibility separate from that of its parent publication, WoodenBoat-a slant toward travel, cruising, and economy of ownership.

feeds.title: Coeur Custom Blog
feeds.description: Owner Duane Hagadone grew up on Lake Coeur d'Alene and took command of his first boat at age 5, a 12-foot Larson with a 5hp Johnson motor. His passion for boats has never ceased, growing over the years to serve as the inspiration and vision for the Coeur Customs team to craft some of the most beautiful boats ever made. Learn more about some of the key members that assist with boat design and concepts, and see why we're the best to launch your legend.

feeds.title: CCWBRA Blog
feeds.description: The CCWBRA was founded in 2010 to encourage and organize racing in the Cocktail Class Runabout. Based on the outboard racer SKUA, an 8 ft. plywood skimmer designed in 1939 by Charles MacGregor, the Cocktail Class Runabout is an economical, easily constructed, and exciting runabout. It is ideal for racing at all skill levels and ages. The Cocktail Class Wooden Boat Racing Association has its origins in the cottage racing clubs of the 1950s when small towns across the country were hosting outboard races for family-built boats and stock outboards.

feeds.title: Modern Wooden Boat Blog
feeds.description: My name is Cristian Pilo, I was born in 1971 in Sardinia, Italy. I'm professionally involved in boat design for homebuilders since 2005. My philosophy is to produce plans that will lead to the building of modern, sporty-looking, sturdy, and reliable boats, with a proper balance between performance and safety on the sea.

feeds.title: Smithy's Boatshed Blog
feeds.description: I've had a long career building, repairing and restoring wooden boats, and although I've retired from commercial work I can't stop building boats. This site shows a lot of the boats I have worked on, as well as the current one I'm building. There's stuff also about my years of teaching boatbuilding, about boat festivals and about the history of the eighteen-footers and open boat racing in Sydney.

feeds.title: Dan Lee Boatbuilding Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to my boat-building blog. Boats and wood have both been passions of mine since a very young age and I love the combination where the two meet. In this section of my website, I select a project that I have been working on and highlight it in more detail and explain the process I followed. I hope you find the content interesting. I will also be posting the latest news on what is happening with Dan Lee Boatbuilding.

feeds.title: Hudson River Maritime Museum Blog
feeds.description: The Hudson River Maritime Museum is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization dedicated to the preservation and interpretation of the maritime history of the Hudson River, its tributaries, and related industries.

feeds.title: Wooden Boats for Veterans Blog
feeds.description: WBFV uses the magic of wooden boat sailing as a pathway for restoring health and well-being to veterans and their families. WBFV provides sailing and restoration instruction, teaching new skills in the community. Through common purpose and teamwork, veterans rediscover inner strengths and share in camaraderie.
